\n<Messenger>Commander, there's news from outside!
\n<Mariano Trias>What's the news?
\n<Messenger>Much news, commander. From Manila to Nueva Ecija.
\n<Mariano Trias>One at a time, then.
\n<Messenger>First — they say a general named Llanera in Nueva Ecija
has also risen up against the Spanish.
\n<Messenger>He has three thousand men with him. They attacked San Isidro — the
capital.
\n<Mariano Trias>Continue.
\n<Messenger>Second — Tandang Sora... she has been deported to Guam.
With her are 171 other prisoners.
\n<Messenger>They say she was double-chained when they put her on
the ship.
\n<Mariano Trias>That is the price of resistance.
\n<Messenger>And third, commander... four of our brothers were executed
at Luneta. At Bagumbayan.
\n<Messenger>Yesterday morning — arrested after the battle at
San Juan. Shot in front of everyone.
\n<Mariano Trias>What are their names?
\n<Messenger>Sancho Valenzuela... Ramon Peralta... Modesto Rivera...
and Eugenio Silvestre.
\n<Floranter>This does not end with one battle, does it?
\n<Mariano Trias>Yesterday you were two men with no name here in Cavite.
\n<Mariano Trias>Today — you are known. Do not waste it.

\n<Messenger>Don Mariano!
\n<Mariano Trias>What is it?
\n<Messenger>Don Mariano. At Fort San Felipe. This morning.
The Messenger stuggles in between breaths, handing a
letter to Mariano Trias.
\n<Mariano Trias>Maximiano Gregorio. Gregorio Bautista.
Severino Lapidario. Ambrosio Lucas. Alfonso de Ocampo.
Agapito Conchu. Maximo Inocencio. Victoriano Luciano.
Jose Lallana. Eugenio Pena. Feliciano Cabuco.
Hugo Perez. Antonio de San Agustin.
Each name lands like a stone dropped in water. Trias'
face darkens each time.
\n<Mariano Trias>They were not captured in battle. They were taken
from their homes, loaded into carts, and executed at
Fort San Felipe.
\n<Mariano Trias>Do you know why Thirteen?
\n<Mariano Trias>Because of fear.
\n<Mariano Trias>They wanted the Caviteños to count.
\n<Mariano Trias>Thirteen in one day — so everyone would know:
if you fight, this is what happens to you.
\n<Mariano Trias>That is why we must win. Because if we lose...
it will not be just thirteen who die.
On 12 September 1896, Spanish authorities executed
thirteen Caviteños at Fort San Felipe, accused of
complicity in the revolution. They were not soldiers
killed in battle; they were civilians — landowners,
professionals, ordinary citizens — executed as a
deliberate warning to terrify the province into
submission. A monument to the Thirteen Martyrs stands
in Cavite City today.

\n<Florante>Now... there is no one left to tell the truth.
